newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Taiwan's SinoPac sets FRCD.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Taiwan's SinoPac sets FRCD.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered a couple of new issues on Wednesday, notably a US$60 million floating rate certificate of deposit for Taiwan's SinoPac.
The US$60 million three-year certificates were launched at par to float at 20 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return is 26 basis points for top tier managers. Merrill Lynch is arranger and bookrunner.
Bankers said they were keen on the bank itself but not so enthusiastic about the pricing.
"We think the pricing is quite tight. Even for a two-year issue, this pricing might be too aggressive," said a syndicate manager at a Japanese bank.
While it is one of Taiwan's newer, smaller banks, Bank SinoPac is considered one of the more aggressive in seeking new business.
Last October, the bank acquired California's Far East National Bank for US$85 million in a bid to develop a regional role on both sides of the Pacific.
The purchase marked the first time a Taiwan bank directly acquired a U.S. bank.
"The bank itself has positioned itself very well," the syndicate manager said, adding "most of the staff have come from Citibank."
"SinoPac also has bet on the right market, consumer financing, and its bad loan ratio is low. It is a good one among all the Taiwan new banks," she said.
Despite the narrow pricing, bankers said the issue may place well because of its rarity value.
At the time of its purchase of Far East National Bank, SinoPac executive officer Paul Lo told Reuters that the bank would consider issuing floating rate notes to pay for the acquisition.
But Merrill Lynch said proceeds of the FRCD will be used for general purposes.
In other news, Bank Internasional Indonesia launched through its Cayman Islands branch a five-year US$35 million FRCD via arranger and bookrunner HSBC Markets.
The certificates pay a margin of 85 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in of 109 basis points to co-lead managers.
The borrower set a five year FRCD puttable after three years last August that paid 96.67 basis points.

Indonesian company SMM Finance has priced its three-year floating rate note issue at 225 basis points over LIBOR, right in the middle of the 220 to 230 basis points range indicated when the issue launched in January.
The issue was increased to US$190 million from US$150 million, arranger Peregrine Fixed Income said. AB Capital Markets was the other arranger.
On the loan side, bankers said Indonesia's Indah Kiat Pulp and Paper has mandated BA ASia and Fuji Singapore to arrange a US$400 million laon facility.
Proceeds will be used for refinancing previous debt.
In news from China, Guangdong Finance Trust and Investment Co has mandated Societe Generale Asia and Hong Kong Bank China Services to arrange a US$85 million loan facility.
